articles.headline: Rescatados 17 tripulantes del pesquero gallego «Génesis» tras embarrancar en las Orcadas
articles.subtitle: El barco, de la compañía ribeirense Basoñas Mar, golpeó unas rocas al amanecer junto al Old Man of Hoy. La meteorología y los acantilados impidieron llegar por mar, así que los marineros salieron por aire.
articles.body:
Los 17 tripulantes del pesquero gallego Génesis fueron evacuados este jueves por vía aérea después de que el barco embarrancase junto al Old Man of Hoy, un acantilado de las islas Orcadas, al norte de Escocia. El buque emitió la señal de socorro poco después de las 7.30 horas, tras golpear unas rocas.

En el operativo participaron helicópteros de los servicios de Guardacostas de Sumburgh y Stornoway, el bote salvavidas de Stromness de la RNLI, equipos terrestres de Kirkwall y St Margaret's Hope y un avión de patrulla de la Royal Air Force. También se desvió de su ruta el Hamnavoe, un ferry de pasajeros, para prestar apoyo a la evacuación.

## Rescate imposible por mar

Las condiciones meteorológicas y la posición del pesquero, encajado junto a una pared rocosa, impidieron que los equipos llegasen hasta él por mar. Los marineros fueron izados por aire y trasladados después a tierra. Medios británicos, desde el semanario local The Orcadian hasta la BBC, siguieron durante horas un rescate que se cerró sin heridos.

El Génesis pertenece a la compañía ribeirense Basoñas Mar. La zona del Old Man of Hoy es un paso habitual de la flota gallega que faena en el Atlántico norte, donde el mal tiempo y una costa recortada convierten cualquier avería en una emergencia de primer orden.

articles.headline: La prospección geofísica en Punta do Cabo descubre un segundo recinto en el castro de Burela
articles.subtitle: El escáner del CSIC, con drones y sensores, revela que el yacimiento tiene más de una línea defensiva y una extensión mayor de la esperada. El Concello quiere expropiar los terrenos.
articles.body:
El estudio geofísico que el Concello de Burela encargó al CSIC en el castro de Punta do Cabo ha localizado un segundo recinto, según los resultados presentados esta semana. Los trabajos, dirigidos por el investigador Pastor Fábrega, del Instituto de Ciencias del Patrimonio, se hicieron sin remover tierra ni tocar las construcciones.

El equipo combinó vuelos de dron con sensores LiDAR y multiespectrales y prospecciones del subsuelo. Esa mezcla permite reconstruir en tres dimensiones la estructura del poblado y detectar murallas, fosos, terrazas y accesos que hoy quedan ocultos por la vegetación. El hallazgo de una segunda línea obliga a revisar al alza el tamaño del asentamiento.

## Un castro más grande de lo que parecía

El yacimiento, situado sobre la Punta do Cabo, apenas ha sido excavado. La campaña de este año buscaba precisamente saber dónde acaba: el espacio arqueológico no termina donde acaban las viviendas, sino que puede incluir defensas, áreas de actividad y terrenos ligados al aprovechamiento del entorno. La zona es conocida además por haber devuelto uno de los torques de oro más notables de la arqueología gallega.

El Ayuntamiento ha anunciado su intención de expropiar los terrenos para que pasen a ser de titularidad pública y puedan visitarse. La prospección se autorizó con permiso arqueológico de la Xunta y con las autorizaciones para los vuelos de drones.

articles.headline: Miguel Fernández presenta en A Milagrosa «Lugo 10», su estrategia para la próxima década
articles.subtitle: El candidato socialista a la Alcaldía arranca en el barrio una ronda de encuentros vecinales con un plan centrado en vivienda, barrios, rural y servicios de cercanía.
articles.body:
El candidato del PSOE a la alcaldía de Lugo, Miguel Fernández, presentó este jueves en la Praza da Milagrosa su estrategia de ciudad para la próxima década, bautizada como Lugo 10. El acto reunió al tejido asociativo y vecinal del barrio y sirvió de arranque para una ronda de encuentros que el socialista llevará durante los próximos meses por barrios y parroquias del municipio.

El documento aborda vivienda, servicios públicos, cuidados, movilidad, barrios, rural, medio ambiente, patrimonio y actividad económica, e incluye, según la presentación, grandes actuaciones de infraestructura y facilidades de acceso a la vivienda.

Fernández defendió que el plan se construya escuchando a los vecinos. «Queremos percorrer cada recuncho do municipio, estar cos veciños, escoitar as súas demandas e explicarlles tamén cal é a nosa visión para o futuro de Lugo. Un proxecto de cidade non se pode facer desde un despacho», dijo durante la presentación.

El candidato socialista quiere conectar las necesidades actuales de la ciudad con los retos de la próxima década, en un momento en el que la vivienda se ha convertido en el asunto central del debate político gallego y estatal.

articles.headline: El Gobierno mantiene la votación de los decretos de vivienda pese al ultimátum de Junts
articles.subtitle: El Ejecutivo rechaza retirar los dos textos y los somete al pleno extraordinario de este viernes, donde el «no» de los independentistas amenaza con tumbarlos.
articles.body:
El Gobierno no retirará ninguno de los dos decretos de vivienda que el Congreso vota este viernes en un pleno extraordinario. La decisión mantiene los textos en el orden del día pese al ultimátum de Junts, que tras reunir a su dirección anunció que votará en contra de ambos si el Ejecutivo no los retira y abre una nueva negociación.

Fuentes del Ejecutivo confirmaron que no habrá marcha atrás. «Ha llegado la hora de la verdad. PP, Vox y Junts deben elegir: o están con la mayoría social o con los especuladores», dijo Pedro Sánchez, que reivindicó que las medidas son fruto de meses de conversaciones con los grupos parlamentarios.

## Caceroladas frente a los ayuntamientos

Horas antes, miles de personas se concentraron con cacerolas y sartenes frente a los ayuntamientos de Madrid, Barcelona y otras capitales para exigir la convalidación de los decretos. Los Sindicatos de Inquilinas cifraron en 2.000 los manifestantes en la plaza de Cibeles y en 800 los reunidos en Sant Jaume. En Madrid se sumaron los acampados en la Puerta del Sol desde el sábado.

Junts exige rehacer los textos para incluir sus demandas, entre ellas la regulación del alquiler de temporada. El PNV dio un apoyo crítico al decreto más amplio y un «no» al de la renovación automática del alquiler. Con ese mapa, lo previsible es que ambas normas decaigan este viernes.

articles.headline: Alerta roja por lluvias en Valencia y Castellón: 359.896 alumnos sin clase y trenes suspendidos
articles.subtitle: La Generalitat lanzó un Es-Alert por «peligro extraordinario» y Renfe cortó la larga distancia entre Cataluña y la Comunidad Valenciana, además de los servicios de Valencia.
articles.body:
La Generalitat Valenciana elevó a roja la alerta por lluvias desde las 18 horas del jueves en el interior norte y el litoral de Castellón y el litoral de Valencia, por «peligro extraordinario». A las 10.02 de la mañana envió un Es-Alert a los móviles pidiendo evitar desplazamientos, alejarse de barrancos y subir a plantas superiores si subía el agua.

La medida dejó sin clase a 359.896 alumnos de 104 municipios, desde colegios e institutos hasta la universidad. Una treintena de ayuntamientos suspendió la actividad lectiva ya el jueves por la tarde y la mantuvo este viernes.

Renfe suprimió desde las 18.00 horas los trenes de larga distancia del Corredor Mediterráneo que unen Cataluña y la Comunidad Valenciana. Entre los afectados, el Alvia Córdoba-Barcelona, dos Euromed entre Alicante y Barcelona, el Euromed Figueres-Alicante y un Intercity Valencia-Barcelona. También se suspendieron los Cercanías y la Media Distancia en Valencia.

La Generalitat mantuvo activado el dispositivo preventivo y pidió a la población seguir los avisos oficiales. Los barrancos y embalses del interior de Castellón eran los puntos de mayor vigilancia.

articles.headline: Los Reyes visitarán Ceuta y Melilla el 13 y 14 de octubre, la primera visita de un jefe del Estado en 20 años
articles.subtitle: Felipe VI y Letizia viajan a las dos ciudades autónomas sin Sánchez y con el Gobierno esperando una «respuesta» de Marruecos, mientras Moncloa desmonta la versión de Vivas.
articles.body:
Los reyes Felipe VI y Letizia visitarán Ceuta y Melilla el 13 y 14 de octubre, respectivamente. La visita, consensuada entre la Zarzuela y el Ejecutivo, será la primera de un jefe del Estado a las dos ciudades autónomas en veinte años y el debut de los monarcas en ambas.

El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, no acompañará a los Reyes. El viaje pretende «normalizar» la presencia de la Corona en Ceuta y Melilla, según fuentes de la Zarzuela. La agenda se dará a conocer en los próximos días.

El anuncio llegó en plena polémica por la gestión de la crisis migratoria. Moncloa hizo público el registro de nueve llamadas entre el presidente y el de Ceuta, Juan Vivas, para desmontar su versión: «Hubo nueve y todas fueron atendidas», señalaron fuentes del Ejecutivo.

Según el Gobierno, España espera ahora una «respuesta» de Marruecos y el Rey no llamará a Mohamed VI antes del viaje. Felipe VI lleva desde su proclamación en 2014 expresando su deseo de acudir a las ciudades autónomas.

articles.headline: Más de tres millones de hogares con tarifa regulada de gas devolverán con intereses la ayuda del tope
articles.subtitle: El límite del 15% a la subida de la TUR entra en vigor y genera una deuda que los clientes amortizarán en sus facturas: unos 100 millones solo entre octubre y diciembre.
articles.body:
El tope del 15% a la subida del precio del gas en la tarifa regulada (TUR) entró en vigor este jueves 1 de octubre y se mantendrá durante dos revisiones trimestrales, hasta el 31 de marzo. La medida evita el sablazo en el recibo de este invierno a más de tres millones de hogares, pero no es una subvención.

A diferencia de la crisis energética de 2022, cuando el Estado cargó unos 600 millones a los Presupuestos, esta vez no hay dinero público. La norma funciona como un «compre ahora y pague después»: la diferencia entre el precio real del gas y lo que figura en la factura se acumula como una deuda que el consumidor devolverá después, con intereses.

El desfase generado solo entre octubre y diciembre rondará los 100 millones de euros, según cálculos del sector, y los clientes empezarán a amortizarlo a partir de enero. Los hogares que se pasen al mercado libre antes de tiempo tendrán que abonar un finiquito obligatorio.

El decreto se publicó el miércoles en el BOE. Las comercializadoras —Naturgy, Iberdrola, Endesa y TotalEnergies— recuperarán el préstamo en las facturas de 2027, cuando el gas baje.

articles.headline: Las nuevas normas de la DGT ya están en vigor: casco en patinete, guantes en moto y uso del arcén
articles.subtitle: La reforma del Reglamento General de Circulación, aprobada en junio, protege a los usuarios vulnerables y cambia reglas para motoristas, ciclistas y patinetes.
articles.body:
El paquete que modifica el Reglamento General de Circulación, aprobado por el Consejo de Ministros el pasado junio y publicado en el BOE el 26 de junio, es obligatorio desde este jueves 1 de octubre. El objetivo declarado es proteger a los usuarios vulnerables: peatones, ciclistas, motoristas y usuarios de vehículos de movilidad personal.

Para motoristas y ciclomotores hay dos cambios de peso. El calzado deberá ser cerrado en cualquier vía, también para el pasajero, con multa de 200 euros por considerarse infracción grave. Y las motos podrán usar el arcén derecho en retenciones, siempre que el tramo esté señalizado y sin superar los 30 kilómetros por hora.

Los usuarios de patinetes y VMP tendrán que llevar casco, y la reforma introduce además cambios para los ciclistas. La DGT busca así reducir la siniestralidad del colectivo más expuesto en ciudad.

Las nuevas obligaciones pillaron por sorpresa a buena parte de los conductores, que se enteraron de su entrada en vigor el mismo día. Desde Tráfico recuerdan que las sanciones ya se aplican.

articles.headline: Drumcree talks end without agreement as unionists move to remove four Sinn Féin ministers
articles.subtitle: Sir Chris Bryant says his door stays open after two hours at Hillsborough, while the DUP and UUP back TUV motions against ministers who joined the Portadown protest and the PSNI puts the policing bill at £3m.
articles.body:
Talks at Hillsborough Castle between the Portadown Orange Order, the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition and the Northern Ireland Secretary ended on Thursday night without agreement. Sir Chris Bryant told reporters: «I think this is the end of these conversations. We haven't come to a settled agreement, and it's a shame, but my door remains open.»

A fresh legal bid by the GRRC to stop the march was due to be heard on Friday but has been postponed until Monday to allow talks to continue.

## Motions at Stormont

Unionist parties have united behind TUV Section 30 motions seeking to remove four Sinn Féin ministers from office for a year. The targets are First Minister Michelle O'Neill and ministers Liz Kimmins, John O'Dowd and Caoimhe Archibald, all of whom attended Sunday's road-block protest. The DUP's 26 MLAs and the UUP's eight put the motions well past the 30-signature threshold. They need cross-community support to succeed, which they will not get, so the debate is symbolic.

The PSNI chief constable told the Policing Board that five days of the standoff have cost £3m, against an annual operations budget of about £930m. UUP leader Jon Burrows has written to the Secretary of State asking Westminster to cover the bill, citing the £4m given to the PSNI after the summer race riots. SDLP MP Colum Eastwood, meanwhile, urged Labour delegates in Liverpool to stand with Garvaghy Road residents.

articles.headline: Fires break out at French schools as student protests spiral into «urban violence»
articles.subtitle: Nearly 1,950 arrests and 305 injured police in a single day as the prime minister calls a crisis cabinet meeting, with about 900 blockades hitting high schools over staffing, class sizes and crumbling buildings.
articles.body:
Fires broke out at several French schools on Thursday as students blockaded education institutions nationwide over funding and studying conditions. Blazes were reported at two high schools in Nantes, and another was filmed engulfing the entrance of a school in the northern city of Rouen. The interior ministry said 1,949 people had been arrested and 305 police officers injured in a single day.

About 900 demonstrations, blockades and related incidents were under way outside high schools around the country. Students are protesting over a lack of teachers and staff, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings; university students joined on Thursday with similar demands.

The government described the escalation as «urban violence» and the prime minister called a crisis cabinet meeting, with many schools switching to online classes. Clashes between riot police and demonstrators were reported in several cities, including Saint-Denis, north of Paris.

The movement began over school conditions and has grown quickly since the start of the academic year, catching the government off guard.

articles.headline: Putin warns Russia will use «all weapons» to defend Kaliningrad
articles.subtitle: Moscow sends NATO a diplomatic note as the Kremlin claims the West is preparing a blockade of the Baltic exclave; Putin also concedes Ukrainian strikes have shaved 1% off Russian GDP.
articles.body:
Vladimir Putin has said Russia will use every weapon at its disposal, including nuclear ones, if it considers its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad to have come under direct attack. The Russian president insisted Moscow was «not threatening anyone» and was merely responding to Western statements that Russia was preparing for war in 2029 or 2030.

Throughout the week Russia has accused NATO of preparing to blockade its territory, which borders Lithuania and Poland, and sent a diplomatic note warning that it would be prepared to use nuclear weapons if the West tried to cut Kaliningrad off from the rest of Russia. NATO has sought to calm the situation, stressing that its posture is defensive.

Putin also said Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure had shaved about 1% off Russia's GDP — a rare public concession on the economic cost of the war. He said Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully.

The exchange is one of the sharpest escalations in rhetoric over the exclave in recent months. Kaliningrad is sandwiched between two NATO members and hosts a heavy Russian military presence.

articles.headline: UK in talks with allies over emergency diesel reserves as Trump threatens export ban
articles.subtitle: Treasury secretary Scott Bessent tells Europe to ready its stockpiles, arguing US farmers and truckers «should not be left carrying the burden» as prices soar before the midterms.
articles.body:
Britain is in talks with European allies about releasing emergency diesel stockpiles after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel. Ministers held discussions about drawing down EU countries' reserves as the White House weighs a ban on diesel exports.

The US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, urged Europe to immediately ready and release such supplies, arguing that US «farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden» as prices soar. Diesel costs have surged because of the war with Iran, putting the issue at the top of voters' minds before November's midterm elections.

The squeeze is uneven. Crude exports through the strait of Hormuz have largely returned to pre-war levels as exporters find workarounds, but flows of refined products such as diesel remain constrained. The UK does not refine enough diesel to meet domestic demand: about a third of its imports last year came from the US.

Trump has said he may also ask European countries to release some of their reserves directly.

articles.headline: Tennessee halts executions for the year after Christa Pike survives two lethal injections
articles.subtitle: The 50-year-old is in critical condition in hospital and her lawyers want her death sentence commuted, while the governor orders a third-party review into what went wrong.
articles.body:
Christa Pike is in «critical condition, receiving life-saving care» in hospital after surviving two lethal injection attempts in Tennessee, her lawyer Randy Spivey said on Thursday. «We don't have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment, but we do know that she is alive right now,» he told reporters.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer a year earlier. She had asked to be executed by a female firing squad, fearing a «prolonged, painful and traumatic» death, an option Tennessee does not allow.

Governor Bill Lee has halted executions in the state for the rest of the year and ordered a third-party review. Pike's lawyers are now asking for her sentence to be commuted.

The case has raised hard questions about lethal injection protocols and about how Tennessee handled a matter that had already been through years of legal battles.

articles.headline: Algeria adopts the death penalty for arsonists after a summer of deadly wildfires
articles.subtitle: The national assembly votes through a bill that also makes child abduction a capital offence, while the official toll of 12 dead is disputed by independent outlets.
articles.body:
Algeria has adopted a law imposing the death penalty on people convicted of arson of forests or fields after a series of wildfires swept parts of the country. Members of the national assembly voted the bill through on Thursday; it also makes child abduction a capital offence.

Capital punishment had remained in the Algerian penal code for some offences, but no execution has been carried out since 1993. President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the justice ministry to draft the changes after more than 200 people were estimated to have died in blazes in the north-east over the summer.

The official death toll from the fires stands at 12, but independent news outlets believe the figure is much higher. The bill still has to clear the upper house of parliament, where Amnesty International has urged members to reject what it calls regressive legislation expanding the death penalty after three decades without executions.

articles.headline: Kanye West's sold-out St Petersburg concerts cancelled after stadium row
articles.subtitle: Organisers confirm the two Gazprom Arena dates are off; Russia's foreign ministry had called the shows unacceptable because of the rapper's «glorification» of Adolf Hitler.
articles.body:
Two sold-out shows that Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, was due to play in Russia have been cancelled, organisers have confirmed. He had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October — which would have been the biggest show by a western artist since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

In a post on Telegram, the Moscow-based promoter Say Agency said the concerts «will not be able to take place on the scheduled dates» and promised an official statement on the project's future. Ticket refunds will be available from Monday.

Chaos surrounded the gigs for weeks: the venue said in August it had not agreed to host Ye, and Russia's foreign ministry called the planned shows unacceptable over the rapper's «glorification» of Adolf Hitler.

Ye has faced a wave of cancellations and lost commercial partners in recent years over antisemitic remarks.

articles.headline: Lyft to pay $272.5m in California's largest-ever wage theft settlement
articles.subtitle: The ride-hailing firm settles claims it misclassified drivers as contractors, with 87% of the money going back to drivers, and the state's attorney general calling it a landmark win.
articles.body:
Lyft has agreed to pay $272.5 million to settle claims that it stole drivers' wages by mislabelling them as independent contractors rather than employees. California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, called the agreement a «landmark win for workers».

The vast majority of the money — 87% — will go back to drivers. Restitution will be calculated from the hours and miles driven between 5 April 2016 and 15 December 2020, the period covered by a case that dates back to a 2020 lawsuit filed when gig-worker classification was still unresolved.

San Francisco city attorney David Chiu, who joined the case, said it was «the largest wage-and-hour settlement in California history», arguing that misclassification «exploits workers, fuels inequality, and creates an unfair economy».

The deal lands as other states weigh similar actions against gig-economy companies. Gig drivers are now classified as contractors under California law, but the settlement covers the years when that question was still live.

articles.headline: LinkedIn chief Ryan Roslansky to leave Microsoft as Nadella reshapes leadership
articles.subtitle: The Microsoft 365 and LinkedIn executive exits after nearly 18 years, following the departures of gaming head Phil Spencer and Office leader Rajesh Jha earlier this year.
articles.body:
Ryan Roslansky, who led LinkedIn for six years and more recently ran Microsoft 365 as well, will leave the company at the end of 2026. Satya Nadella announced the departure in a memo to employees on Thursday.

«After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky has decided to leave and embark on his next chapter,» Nadella wrote. Roslansky will stay through the end of the calendar year as an adviser and support the transition.

The exit follows a year of churn at the top. Gaming head Phil Spencer and Office chief Rajesh Jha have both left in 2026, and Charlie Bell, the company's head of security, moved into an individual-contributor role.

Nadella used the announcement to restate direction: «With Copilot, we are executing rapidly against our vision to build a new OS for work that spans every mode.» Microsoft has been reorganising around generative AI, with Copilot woven through its productivity products.

articles.headline: New York City becomes the first US city to enforce a «click to cancel» rule
articles.subtitle: The rule, in force since 1 October, obliges businesses to make ending an auto-renewing subscription as easy as starting one, with a city portal for complaints.
articles.body:
New York City's «click to cancel» rule took effect on Thursday, making the city the first municipality in the country to impose such a requirement, according to the mayor's office. Businesses must now make it as easy for customers to end an auto-renewing subscription as it was to sign up.

New York state already requires a cancellation method to be as easy as sign-up, but the city rule gives local authorities their own enforcement power. The city is also launching a consumer portal for complaints, which officials say will not send users into a «chatbot doom loop».

The move fills a gap left by Washington. A federal version of the rule was halted by an appeals court, and the future of a national standard remains unsettled even as more states adopt similar laws.

Subscription businesses now face a patchwork of rules depending on where their customers live — and enforcement in the largest US market.

articles.headline: Apple's rumoured smart home camera will not record any video, Gurman says
articles.subtitle: The device is described as an AI sensor that analyses what happens at home and reports it, rather than a conventional security camera with footage you can review.
articles.body:
Apple's long-rumoured smart home camera will have «no video recording», according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, speaking on his new Power On podcast. He described the product instead as a sensor capable of «analyzing your environment in your home» using AI.

«This is going to be the first mainstream home video security camera that doesn't give you any footage,» Gurman said. That would place it in a different category from Ring and Google Nest hardware, where recorded clips are the core feature.

Reports describe the device internally as J450, expected to work alongside a smart home hub Apple is rumoured to launch next month. The pitch appears to be privacy: the camera understands what is happening without storing video for users to watch back.

Whether buyers will accept a security camera that cannot show them the break-in is the open question. Apple has declined to comment on unreleased products.

articles.headline: Amazon's new Kindle drops the raised bezel for a thinner, lighter e-reader
articles.subtitle: The whole range is refreshed — a 6-inch base Kindle, a 7-inch Paperwhite and a 7-inch Colorsoft — with an aluminium build and a flush display, ahead of the Kindle's 20th birthday.
articles.body:
Amazon has given the Kindle its biggest physical redesign in years, introducing a refreshed line-up built around a deceptively simple idea: removing the raised bezel. The new models have a front-flush display, making them thinner and lighter than the devices they replace.

The range includes a new 6-inch base Kindle, a 7-inch Paperwhite and a 7-inch Colorsoft, plus Signature Editions of the latter two and Kids versions across the family. The new Kindles also move to an aluminium build.

The launch comes ahead of the Kindle's 20th anniversary in 2027, which Amazon says it will mark throughout the year. The devices are rolling out in the US, Canada, the UK, Japan, Australia and several European and Middle Eastern markets.

For a category that had settled into small annual refreshes, a full redesign is a statement — and an attempt to keep readers from drifting to tablets and phones.

articles.headline: OpenAI fires three researchers over mishandling of «sensitive information»
articles.subtitle: At least two of the sacked staff worked on safety research, and the company says the data was shared with an outside group that analyses AI models.
articles.body:
OpenAI has fired three researchers for allegedly mishandling information, including work involving an external organisation that analyses artificial intelligence models. The company did not name those dismissed, but at least two of them were involved in safety research.

«Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work,» a spokesperson told the BBC.

The firings land in the middle of a public argument about AI safety and the risks the technology may pose to humanity. The episode also raises uncomfortable questions for a company whose pitch has long included keeping frontier models under careful internal control.

OpenAI's handling of the case is likely to be scrutinised both by regulators and by the safety researchers it still employs — the people best placed to see where a breach ends and a disagreement begins.

articles.headline: Google's Guided Vision lets Gemini describe what its camera sees
articles.subtitle: The Gemini Live feature is aimed at people with low vision, who can point a phone at the world, have it described, and ask follow-up questions about what is nearby.
articles.body:
Google has added a Guided Vision feature to Gemini Live that uses a phone's camera to describe a user's surroundings. People with low vision can point the device at a scene, have Gemini describe what is nearby and then ask follow-up questions.

It builds on visual guidance work Google debuted alongside the Pixel 10, which highlights objects spotted by the camera. The new mode pushes further into accessibility, surfacing details such as fine print that a user may not be able to read.

The obvious question is whether users can trust a model to describe the world accurately when its description is the only version they get. A confident misreading of a label or a sign is worse than no help at all.

Google has spent a year building accessibility features into Gemini, and appears to be preparing more granular controls, including ways to switch camera-guided modes off.

articles.headline: Decision models flood the web as Amazon and Cloudflare ship Jev-style AI
articles.subtitle: AWS releases Strands Decider 2B while Cloudflare open-sources Clef and Clef-flash, part of a shift toward small models built to return typed answers instead of chat.
articles.body:
Two of the largest cloud providers shipped decision models within a day of each other, a sign that AI developers increasingly want intelligence shaped for automation rather than conversation. Amazon Web Services' Strands Labs released Strands Decider 2B, a model inspired by TypeSafe's Jev.

Cloudflare open-sourced its own pair — Clef and Clef-flash — hosted on Workers AI for high-speed classification and agentic workflows. It also launched a reinforcement learning platform so developers can fine-tune decision models on their own data.

Decision models return structured output, such as typed probabilities, instead of prose. That makes them cheap to run, easy to chain inside software and useful for the unglamorous decisions — routing, ranking, filtering — that agents make thousands of times in a session.

The rush to clone the idea suggests the Jev format may become a default interface between agents and the systems they control.

articles.headline: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust suits over Google's AI Overviews
articles.subtitle: US district judge Amit Mehta rules the publishers' claims «fail to get out of the starting gate», a blow to attempts to treat AI summaries as a competition problem.
articles.body:
A US judge has dismissed antitrust lawsuits brought by Chegg and Penske Media, the parent company of Rolling Stone, over Google's AI Overviews. Both had claimed that Google's AI search features drove traffic away from their sites.

In a ruling on Wednesday, US district judge Amit Mehta in Washington said the publishers' claims that Google's business practices violate antitrust law «fail to get out of the starting gate».

The decision removes one legal route for publishers hurt by AI-generated answers, but it does not settle the underlying argument about whether search engines can summarise and reuse content at scale.

Chegg has been among the most vocal complainants, arguing that AI Overviews gutted its traffic. Similar grievances are being pursued through copyright claims rather than competition law.

articles.headline: Shopify's Canvas lets merchants build a store by chatting with its AI agent
articles.subtitle: The new design surface works with Sidekick: describe what you want, watch the changes land in real time, and go from nothing to a custom storefront in about 20 minutes.
articles.body:
Shopify has introduced Canvas, a site-building surface that lets merchants set up and customise an online store by chatting with Sidekick, the company's AI agent. Changes appear in a visual workspace as they happen, with the agent editing theme code behind the scenes.

The company says the tool is aimed at people with no design or coding experience. Ben Sehl, Shopify's director of product, said that when he built Kotn twelve years ago it took him two weeks to get a rough store working; he claims a merchant can now build a fully custom store in about twenty minutes.

Canvas fits a broader shift in which AI agents stop answering questions and start operating software — editing files, running workflows and producing finished artefacts. Shopify is betting merchants will let an agent touch the storefront itself.

Canvas is rolling out to merchants over the coming days.
